blind_spots: Privileged pods admitted in namespaces with a permissive Pod Security level (or exempted users/namespaces) are not denied and therefore not detected here.
Requests whose audit body was not logged (audit level Metadata) may lack risk flags; the rule then relies on the violation text (confidence medium).
Violations of other Pod Security controls (runAsNonRoot, seccomp, ...) alone are not in scope.
Audit pipeline outages (OTel collector, gateway) hide denials; see collector health.
rule.description: A request to create a pod (or add an ephemeral container) asking for privileged mode, host namespaces (hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC), hostPath volumes or dangerous added capabilities was rejected with HTTP 403 because it violates the namespace's Pod Security Standard. The control worked; the alert records who tried to run a privileged workload, where, and with which settings. Evidence is the kube-apiserver audit event (ResponseComplete stage) normalised by the OTLP audit pipeline.
false_positives: An administrator deploying a legitimate node agent (CNI, CSI driver, log collector) into a namespace whose Pod Security level does not allow it; the fix is an exempt or privileged namespace, not a suppression.
Server-side dry runs (kubectl --dry-run=server) are denied the same way; they are alerted (reconnaissance of the admission policy) with features.dry_run = true.

Controllers retrying a privileged Deployment/DaemonSet in a restricted namespace produce one denial per retry, and therefore one alert per audit id (identity is the audit id per PLAN 5.3); the alerts share the same group (cluster|namespace|user).
rule.title: Privileged pod denied by Pod Security admission
